title: Orchid Peak hybrid GPU onramp discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Orchid Peak to explore a hybrid GPU onramp partnership. Covered Orchid Peak's heterogeneous on-prem GPU fleet, driver and image constraints, latency/cost targets, security and compliance concerns (SAML/KMS/audit logs), and go-to-market alignment. Agreed next steps: share architecture docs, run benchmark profile, draft reseller economics, and schedule technical deep dive week of 10/26.
next_steps: Redwood: share private partner pack + architecture diagram (Ava) - due 2026-10-22
Orchid Peak: provide sample workload and perf targets (Priya) - due 2026-10-23
Schedule SE deep-dive + access window for benchmarking (Diego and Priya) - proposed week of 2026-10-26
NDA routing for resale + legal contacts (Simon) - due 2026-10-29
action_items: Diego Martinez - prepare short perf checklist and bench harness; include heterogenous GPU guidance - 2026-10-24
Ava Chen - draft partner economics / go-to-market proposal and share reseller margin assumptions - 2026-10-25
Priya Rao - export 2 representative workloads (LLM batch + streaming inference) and share input shapes - 2026-10-23
Simon Huang - send procurement contact and preferred NDA template - 2026-10-29
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Nia Patel (Redwood Partner Ops); Lara Singh (Orchid Peak - Head Cloud Infra), Marcus Cole (CTO), Priya Rao (Lead Platform Engineer), Simon Huang (Procurement).

--- Summary / TL;DR ---
Ava: thanks everyone for making time, we wanted to do a quick partner intro and understand Orchid Peak's hybrid onramp use cases and constraints.
Lara: thanks, we run a mix of colo and customer-managed racks, fleet is pretty heterogenous and we'd like an onramp that can route workloads to cloud or to our partners' dedicated enclosures depending on latency and cost.

[00:00:18] Ava: quick agenda, intros, high-level Redwood architecture, then dig into the operational constraints you have, device/driver questions, security, and, um, commercial/go-to-market.
[00:00:34] Marcus: sounds good. also, quick note: our legal person is on another call, so procurement will follow up on NDA.

[00:01:12] Diego: I work as a solutions engineer on hosting and private deployments, so I can jump into runtime compatibility, quantization, and the KV cache behavior when we talk about streaming.
[00:01:26] Priya: great — and for context our fleet is a mix of A100s, H100s, and older V100s in a few customer-managed racks. We're trying to avoid forklift upgrades; we want software-level compatibility and scheduling options.

[00:02:05] Lara: our main drivers are: one, be able to offer customers lower-cost inference for non-latency-sensitive workloads; two, guarantee low-p99 latency for premium customers; three, provide audit logs and SSO integrations for enterprise customers.

[00:02:40] Diego: makes sense. Redwood's runtime supports mixed-precision and quantization-friendly paths. For heterogeneous fleets we usually recommend model variants pinned to capability tiers — so an H100-optimized runtime and a fallback quantized variant for older V100-style nodes. That avoids a costly full fleet refresh.

[00:03:12] Marcus: how transparent is that to the app? can we keep a single API endpoint?
[00:03:24] Diego: yes, same API. Smart routing handles selection by policy — latency first or cost first, with automatic fallback. You can pin customers to a policy or route by token.

[00:04:10] Priya: driver versions have bitten us in the past; our ops team is nervous about CUDA and driver drift across racks. what does Redwood expect for the node image?
[00:04:27] Diego: we provide prebuilt images with tested CUDA stacks and container runtime. For private deployments, customers can opt to run Redwood's agent in their cluster — it tolerates a range of driver versions but we do require a minimum CUDA toolkit and certain NCCL versions for NVLink performance. We'll share the matrix.

[00:05:01] Priya: okay, please share that matrix. also, some of our customers run air-gapped environments where outbound access is restricted. is there an on-prem only control plane option?
[00:05:18] Ava: yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane / air-gapped deployment. There are two modes: VPC-isolated control plane with outbound proxies, or fully air-gapped on-prem bundle. We've done a few regulated-finance deployments.

[00:05:47] Lara: security — SSO and audit logs are table stakes. We need SAML/IdP integration, RBAC at the tenant level, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[00:06:05] Nia: we've got SAML, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. For KMS, we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM providers; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include links to our security pack.

[00:06:34] Marcus: good. what's the observability like — token-level cost breakdowns, or per-model latency histograms?
[00:06:44] Diego: yes to both. Console provides model-level dashboards, per-route latency percentile charts, and token cost breakdowns. For dedicated partners we can surface additional traces and batch-level metrics.

[00:07:20] Priya: on the perf side, we need reproducible benchmarks. Can your bench harness run in our env against our datasets?
[00:07:33] Diego: absolutely — we typically run a short on-site or remote bench: we bring a small harness, you provide representative workloads and network topology, we run baseline and then test with Redwood's batching/caching settings. Results are shared in a spreadsheet.

[00:08:02] Marcus: do you support colocated NVLink topology detection? our racks have some NVLink meshes and some nodes are without it.
[00:08:12] Diego: we have heuristics and runtime flags for NVLink-aware kernel selection. When NVLink is present we default to collective strategies; if not present we fall back to pointwise. We'll need a brief discovery of your interconnects.

[00:08:49] Lara: from a business model perspective, we're thinking of being a reseller for lower-tier workloads and direct co-sell for enterprise. What's your partner pricing and reseller discount approach?
[00:09:05] Ava: usually we offer tiered partner discounts based on committed capacity with a simple rev-share for co-sell. For channel partners we can do referral credits for self-serve onboards. We'll draft options and assumptions.

[00:09:28] Simon: procurement note — our standard is 60-day payment terms, and we prefer a master reseller agreement template. We'll send Simon's template.

[00:09:49] Ava: noted; we'll review. Also worth aligning on support model — 24/7 vs business hours, and escalation path. For Dedicated partners we have SLA-backed latencies and a partner engineering channel.

[00:10:12] Priya: curious about model onboarding — how heavy is it to onboard a custom model variant?
[00:10:22] Diego: onboarding usually takes a few days for a typical open-weight model. We have toolchains to convert checkpoints, run compatibility tests, generate quantization profiles, and produce Redwood-verified performance profiles. If your customers bring proprietary weights we can run onboarding within your environment under NDA.

[00:11:01] Lara: a question about tenant isolation — can we ensure strict separation for customers that require it?
[00:11:12] Diego: yes. Dedicated pools per-tenant is the cleanest. For multi-tenant we have strong namespace isolation, model vaults, and token scoping. We can provide SOC2 audit evidence.

[00:11:45] Priya: latency targets — for premium customers we need p99 < 120ms for 4k token streams. is that realistic on your side?
[00:12:00] Diego: depends on model and batch size. For large decoder models that might be tough on V100 nodes. With H100-class hardware and tuned batch sizes we can hit that. This is where routing policies help — route premium traffic to H100 pool, cheaper traffic to quantized variants.

[00:12:33] Lara: network egress — some of our customers limit egress out of their VPC. If the control plane needs to fetch models or updates, how does that work?
[00:12:46] Nia: we support signed model bundles and on-prem model hosting. The deployment agent can pull from an internal artifact repo or accept offline bundles, so no outbound requirement for runtime. For updates we usually use a signed delta mechanism.

[00:13:22] Marcus: any existing integrations with CNCF runtimes like K3s, K8s distro X, or edge orchestrators?
[00:13:31] Diego: we've validated on standard Kubernetes (1.24+), OpenShift, and a few edge orchestrators. For lightweight distros we recommend our thin agent + containerd. We'll include the compatibility list in the pack.

[00:14:05] Priya: what's the expected footprint for the agent? we've got tight memory constraints on some management nodes.
[00:14:15] Diego: it's a small agent (~100-200MB resident) mostly a shim to the runtime. The heavy lifting is in the inference runtime on the GPU nodes.

[00:14:42] Lara: ok can we talk about support SLAs for patching? we need a predictable patch window and scheduled maintenance windows.
[00:14:55] Ava: yes, we operate on scheduled maintenance windows for private deployments and can align with your change control. For critical security patches we have emergency channels and hotfix delivery.

[00:15:22] Priya: one more ops detail — how do you handle KV cache warmup and cross-tenant cache leakage concerns?
[00:15:33] Diego: KV cache is per-tenant and sharded per-instance. We have strict isolation — no shared cache across tenants. Warmup can be seeded from recent traffic or payload prefixes; we'll share documentation.

[00:15:58] Marcus: ok shifting to go-to-market: do you have enablement materials for partners to self-sell?
[00:16:08] Nia: yes — partner portal, co-branded decks, sales playbooks, and a partner training track. We can do a 2-hour enablement for your GTM and solution engineers.

[00:16:41] Lara: timeline — if we like the bench results we aim to enable reseller offering by end of Q1 2027. Does that fit your roadmap?
[00:16:55] Ava: yes, that's doable. We'll treat this as a Q1 partner activation with initial pilot in late 2026.

[00:17:20] Priya: some technical nitty-gritty — we use Mellanox switches and sometimes have RDMA enabled. Does Redwood runtime need special config for RDMA?
[00:17:34] Diego: we support GPUDirect RDMA stacks; we may need the NIC firmware and RDMA kernel modules in place. We'll surface the recommended NIC drivers and tuning knobs.

[00:18:05] Marcus: any tricky licensing issues for model binaries when reselling?
[00:18:14] Ava: licensing is model-specific. For open models it's straightforward. For customer-provided or commercial models we handle license checks and can enforce model-specific usage via policy. Legal will need to align on MSA addenda.

[00:18:40] Simon: on procurement again — we'll need clear pricing tiers and minimum commit requirements for partner discounts.

[00:18:51] Ava: we'll draft a simple tiered proposal; one for reseller referral (no commit), one for committed capacity with reserved blocks, and a co-sell rev share for enterprise deals.

[00:19:18] Lara: curious if you have any partner references in regulated industries? that would help selling into our finance customers.

[00:19:28] Nia: yes, we have two references in finance and one in healthcare with air-gapped deployments; we'll share redacted case studies and reference contacts.

[00:19:52] Priya: there's some hesitation internally about operational burden. can you show an example onboarding runbook?
[00:20:03] Diego: yep we'll include a runbook with the partner pack — steps for image bootstrap, agent install, model onboarding, and perf validation. Typically 3-5 days for an initial pilot if the environment is provisioned.

[00:20:42] Marcus: do you expose billing APIs so we can embed costs into our portal?
[00:20:51] Nia: yes, metering APIs and usage webhooks. Partners can pull token-level usage and reconcile invoices.

[00:21:16] Lara: any gotchas for air-gapped clients when they want to use Redwood's model catalog?
[00:21:27] Diego: for air-gapped we provide signed model bundles and you can seed an internal catalog. The main thing is licensing and ensuring the bundle update mechanism is compatible with your patch controls.

[00:21:56] Priya: ok, last technical: do you support container runtimes besides docker? containerd and crio?
[00:22:05] Diego: yes containerd and CRI-O are supported; we recommend containerd for our agent images.

[00:22:30] Simon: from procurement side, can we get a sample reseller MSA to speed legal review?
[00:22:39] Ava: yes I'll attach our partner MSA with the partner pack.

[00:22:56] Marcus: great. Any immediate blockers?
[00:23:03] Lara: just internal alignment on support model, and we'll want to run the perf bench to validate p99 numbers.

[00:23:18] Diego: we'll need access window to run bench; suggest a minimal set of nodes and a small dataset to reproduce.

[00:23:32] Priya: agreed. We'll prepare two workloads and a small test cluster slice.

[00:23:47] Ava: perfect. Let's recap next steps.

[00:24:00] Ava (recap): Redwood to share partner pack, architecture diagram, compatibility matrix, runbook, and partner MSA by 10/22. Diego to send perf checklist and bench harness instructions by 10/24. Orchid Peak to share sample workloads and node topology by 10/23. Simon to route procurement contact and NDA template by 10/29. Schedule technical deep-dive week of 10/26 — Nia will coordinate.

[00:24:35] Marcus: sounds good. I'm excited about a hybrid model where we can route premium p99 traffic to H100s and non-critical to quantized V100s.
[00:24:48] Lara: thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.

[00:25:02] Priya: just one more clarifying Q — does Redwood support canary model rollouts?
[00:25:10] Diego: yes, canary and A/B rollouts are supported at the model-version level with automatic fallback policies.

[00:25:30] Ava: ok if we close here, we'll circulate the materials and propose two slots for the week of 10/26 for the deep-dive.
[00:25:42] Simon: thanks, will look out for the NDA and the pricing tiers.

[00:26:00] Meeting end: 16:58 PT
